Israeli Engineering & Construction Workers Stage Walkout, Halting Major Projects

TEL AVIV, June 12 – Thousands of workers in Israel’s Engineering & Construction industry walked off job sites Wednesday, halting work on major infrastructure and housing projects nationwide as part of an ongoing dispute over pay and working conditions.

The strike, organized by the National Union of Building and Engineering Workers, began at 6 a.m. local time, with union leaders saying more than 11,000 workers had joined the walkout. Construction sites in Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Haifa, and Beersheba stood idle as cranes, machinery, and tools went quiet.

Industry analysts said the work stoppage threatens to delay completion timelines for high-profile projects, including residential high-rises, highway expansions, and a light rail extension in central Israel. “This is the busiest season for construction, and every day lost will have a ripple effect on delivery dates and project costs,” said Doron Maimon, an analyst at the Israeli Construction Forum.

Union officials cited rising living costs and stagnant wages as core grievances. “For months, we have tried to negotiate fair terms,” union chair Eliyahu Peretz said at a midday rally in Tel Aviv. “Our members build this country’s future, but their own futures remain uncertain.”

The Israel Engineering Contractors Association urged both sides to return to the negotiating table. “Prolonged disruption will severely impact the sector’s stability,” said CEO Ronit Malka in a statement.

According to the Ministry of Housing and Construction, more than 130 sites are currently affected, with delays expected to escalate if the strike continues. Negotiations between union representatives and employers are ongoing but have yet to yield a resolution.

As of Wednesday evening, the walkout remained in effect, with further talks scheduled for Thursday.
